Summary: Enterprise retail-tech shop building personalization + support agent + reranking for search. Primary risk = throughput/capacity during promotional bursts. POC showed good steady-state throughput (≈1k rps) but queueing and increased tail latency under synthetic spikes to 8-12k rps. Fluxion's core requirement: sub-200ms p95 for customer-facing personalization calls and zero queueing for 30-60s promotional bursts (Black Friday-like).

POC details / quotes: - 1/20 interim: "we saw queueing once traffic hit ~9k; checkout personalization lagged". - 1/28 engineering: Redwood proposed multi-tier routing: reserved dedicated + burst pool + priority tokenization; cost trade-offs discussed. - 2/12 procurement: competitor guaranteed burst isolation via pre-warmed nodes and lower committed price. Fluxion: "short term price and burst SLAs matter more than long-term ops maturity".

Security/Deployment: Strong VPC and KMS requirements; on-prem feasibility requested for isolated campaigns. Security team asked for logs retention policy and an audit trail (tie-in to Redwood audit_logging). Review timeline slipped due to CISO availability.

Current status: Stalled / procurement paused. No active champion in exec team — initial sponsor moved to new role. AE recommends re-open if competitor fails SLA or after fiscal Q3 budget refresh.

Suggested playbook: - Offer a short-term burst-validation pilot with isolated pre-warmed capacity and clear burst SLOs (p95/p99) for 90 days. - Provide SOC2 + KMS integration docs and bespoke retention language for legal. - Introduce cost model showing delta vs competitor for 6/12 month horizons.

CRM shorthand: POC strong steady-state, weak under bursts; security ask in progress; lost momentum to RivalServe on guaranteed burst SLA and price; finance froze. Follow-ups pending, low touch until exec budget review.
